label: Bible Study
prompt: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I _____ him? till seven times?
verse: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
note: Peter thought seven times was generous — Jesus answered with seventy times seven.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Because thy lovingkindness is better than _____, my lips shall praise thee.
verse: Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee.
note: Written in the wilderness of Judah: God's lovingkindness is better than life itself.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And when he had made a _____ of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers' money, and overthrew the tables;
verse: And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers' money, and overthrew the tables;
note: John's temple scene: Jesus made a scourge of small cords and drove out the sheep, the oxen, and the changers.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the LORD had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a _____.
verse: Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the LORD had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.
note: Naaman had rank, victories and the king's favor — and one word that undid it all, until a captive Israelite girl spoke up.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For he _____ the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
verse: For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
note: God 'satisfieth the longing soul' — then Psalm 107 tells rescue stories of wanderers, prisoners, the sick, and storm-tossed sailors.
